articles.description: Lawmakers are hoping to avoid a third shutdown since last September. The stopgap funding measure now heads to the Senate, where it faces an uncertain future.
articles.title: House votes to extend government funding, aiming to avoid an election year shutdown

articles.author: Anastasia Tsioulcas
articles.description: In a House DOGE subcommittee hearing, GOP representatives excoriated the director of the National Museum of American History, following a White House report earlier this month that also criticized her.
articles.title: Smithsonian too focused on 'oppressors and the oppressed,' say House Republicans

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy fired Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi as commander-in-chief of Ukraine's armed forces following days of protests demanding his removal. Zelenskyy appointed Mykhailo Drapatyi as the new army chief.
articles.title: Ukraine's Zelenskyy fires his military chief after protests and names a new one

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The announcement effectively canceled Nicaragua's next elections, originally scheduled for November 2027.
articles.title: Nicaragua's President Ortega says no more elections, extending his 20-year rule

articles.author: Maria Godoy
articles.description: A new study finds that consumers who are paying a premium for foods advertised as made with avocado oil are probably not getting what they think they're buying.
articles.title: Is that food really made with 100% avocado oil? Likely not

articles.author: James Perkins Mastromarino
articles.description: Titans like Resident Evil Requiem and Crimson Desert dominated in the first half of the gaming year, with early-access sequels like Slay the Spire 2 and Subnautica 2 not far behind.
articles.title: The best games of 2026 so far, picked by NPR's staff

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: The movement, which began as a satirical protest, has evolved into a nationwide challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government.
articles.title: India's youth-led Cockroach movement vows to continue protest after police crackdown

articles.author: Kristen Martin
articles.description: Catch the Devil by journalist Pamela Colloff highlights the potentially fatal consequences of a system more concerned with securing convictions than determining the truth and delivering justice.
articles.title: A teen was murdered in 1985. A new book tracks the case through a broken legal system

articles.author: The Associated Press
articles.description: President Donald Trump on Monday imposed 50% tariffs on most Canadian goods, declaring that Canada has unfairly discriminated against American autos, alcohol and dairy products.
articles.title: Trump imposes 50% tariffs on Canadian goods

articles.author: Maansi Srivastava
articles.description: Harrisburg is home to one of the nation's largest communities of Nepali-speaking Bhutanese refugees and their families. Through soccer, generations have found connection, belonging and a way to carry forward a shared history.
articles.title: How soccer brings a Bhutanese community together in Harrisburg, Pa.

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Follow today’s news live

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales premier, Chris Minns, says the state’s Labor party is under threat from One Nation and “we’ve got to fight for those votes”.
Appearing on ABC Radio National this morning, Minns was asked if One Nation was a “racist party”. He said people who had concerns about the levels of immigration weren’t necessarily racist but some of the things Pauline Hanson had said were.
Certainly some of the things Pauline Hanson says are definitely racist, when she said there’s no such thing as a good Muslim. I mean, how else do you characterise that? You’ve got to be straight with people. And that clearly is. But I don’t think everyone who’s supporting them currently is racist at all … And we’ve got to fight for those votes.
I think that we are under threat in a whole bunch of seats as a result of the surge of votes for One Nation … So we’re doing some what we regard as practical commonsense changes to policy in New South Wales.
When people join the Do Not Call Register or unsubscribe from marketing messages, they are making a clear choice. Those choices must be respected – especially given the heightened risks of financial loss and psychological harm from gambling marketing.
The scale and range of these breaches point to serious weaknesses in TAB’s compliance systems.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia news live: Brittany Higgins accuses Hanson of victim-blaming in ‘atrocious’ comments on domestic violence

articles.author: Mark Saunokonoko, Maya Yang, Nadeem Badshah, Tom Ambrose, Taz Ali and Adam Fulton
articles.description:
This blog is now closed. Read our latest full report here.
Lebanon’s president, Joseph Aoun, is due to meet Donald Trump for the first time today as he wraps up a four-day visit to Washington.
The meeting coincides with ongoing US-mediated talks between Lebanon and Israel. The two sides announced a “framework agreement” on 26 June which stipulates the withdrawal of Israeli forces from southern Lebanon as well as the disarmament of Hezbollah.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth estimates rising cost of Iran war now at $37.5bn – as it happened

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement
Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement.
Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Rahul Gandhi briefly detained as cockroach protests rock Delhi

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Measure authorizes spending until 4 December as Republicans seek to avoid volatile issue in election season
The US House of Representatives on Tuesday approved a stopgap measure to head off a government shutdown until early December, with its Republican leaders seeking to defuse a volatile issue in the run-up to the November midterm elections.
The continuing resolution authorizing government spending until 4 December passed by a vote of 220-205, roughly along party lines. It next heads to the Senate, where it will need to win bipartisan support to clear the chamber.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House passes spending bill to head off government shutdown before midterms

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Sgt Angel S Pampersad also believed to be dead in attack that killed two others, raising death toll to 18 troops since start of Iran war
The US military has confirmed that a third service member is believed to be dead in Friday’s attack on a base in Jordan and identified them as Sgt Angel S Rampersad, 28, of New York.
The confirmation brings the death toll to 18 US service members killed since the war began.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US military identifies third service member killed in Iranian attack on Jordan base

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News email

US gas prices have continued to rise since the conflict with Iran resumed this month. According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), a gallon of fuel is now just over $4 – almost a dollar more than a year ago.
It comes as Brent Crude, the international oil benchmark, is now up by almost 2% to $90.92 a barrel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces new tariffs on generic drugs to take effect in 2028 – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
Storm warnings stretch from Florida to Louisiana as Bertha brings heavy rain, flooding risk and possible tornadoes
Tropical Storm Bertha strengthened in the Gulf of Mexico on Tuesday but was expected to weaken this week as it chugs closer to the US, potentially bringing coastal flooding and heavy rain from the Florida Panhandle to Louisiana.
Those areas along the northern Gulf coast were under a tropical storm warning through Wednesday and could see rain and flooding into Thursday morning, the Miami-based National Hurricane Center said. New Orleans also was under a tropical storm warning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tropical Storm Bertha expected to weaken as it moves toward US

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The second circuit overturned the previous decision, saying the judge overstepped authority by intervening before it moved through the immigration court system
A federal appeals panel has reversed a lower court decision ordering the release of pro-Palestinian activist Mohsen Mahdawi, opening the door to the re-arrest of a student protest organizer whom the Trump administration has spent more than a year trying to deport.
Tuesday’s ruling from the second US circuit court of appeals in New York City overturns a previous decision by a federal judge in Vermont, which likened the government’s efforts to expel him and other activists to McCarthyist repression.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Appeals court reverses decision that released pro-Palestinian Columbia activist Mohsen Mahdawi

articles.author: Robert Mackey
articles.description:
Mayor had said he was reviewing ability to execute arrest warrant issued by the ICC for Israeli prime minister
Zohran Mamdani, the New York City mayor, acknowledged on Tuesday he does not have the authority to arrest Benjamin Netanyahu, but urged US federal authorities to do so if the Israeli prime minister visits the US later this year.
“Benjamin Netanyahu is a war criminal, the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people,” Mamdani said in a video posted to social media.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mamdani says New York City does not have legal authority to arrest Netanyahu

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The ribbon-cutting celebration of the Gordie Howe International Bridge is no longer taking place after Trump announced a 50% tariff on Canadian goods
A planned joint US-Canada ceremony Friday celebrating the opening of the Gordie Howe International Bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor, Ontario, is no longer expected to take place after Donald Trump announced a 50% tariff on most Canadian goods.
In announcing the tariffs, the president accused Canada of unfairly discriminating against US automobiles, alcohol and dairy products, escalating tensions with one of the United States’ closest allies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Canada cancels joint bridge-opening celebration with US amid trade tensions

articles.author: Caitlin Cassidy
articles.description:
Police found woman dead in Bentley home and seriously injured girl on nearby highway

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A teenage boy has been charged with murder after he allegedly killed his mother with a knife and stabbed his little sister, who managed to flee to get help.
The 16-year-old boy was charged on Wednesday with one count of murder and one count of attempting to unlawfully kill after police attended a home at Bentley, in Perth’s south-east, on Tuesday morning.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Perth teenager charged with murdering his mother and attempting to kill sister

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington and Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Defense secretary has asked Senate appropriations committee for nearly $88bn more to continue effort
The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth told the Senate on Tuesday that the US-Israel war on Iran had cost $37.5bn so far, as he faced lawmakers furious over the conflict’s soaring price tag and the deaths last week of three American service members.
During an appearance before the Senate appropriations committee, Hegseth, whose opening remarks were repeatedly interrupted by protesters, provided an updated account of the war’s cost – up from previous estimates – and defended the Trump administration’s roughly $88bn supplemental funding request, calling it “urgent, necessary”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth tells Senate war on Iran has so far cost $37.5bn at hearing to request more funds

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Luke Harding in Dnipro
articles.description:
After nationwide protests Oleksandr Syrskyi is to be replaced in reshuffle and popular defence minister returns to government
Volodymyr Zelenskyy has fired Ukraine’s commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi and offered a “prominent position” to the defence minister he sacked last week in a move that sparked nationwide protests.
In a late-night TV address, Zelenskyy said he was appointing Mykhailo Drapatyi, a popular and innovative general, as the new head of Ukraine’s armed forces. Drapatyi would oversee a reorganisation of the army’s command structure, Ukraine’s president said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zelenskyy fires Ukraine’s army chief and offers Fedorov ‘prominent position’

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker
articles.description:
As new prime minister briefs cabinet on ‘cost of living government’, critics ask where money will come from
Andy Burnham is under mounting pressure to explain how he will pay for his policy pledges as he implored his new cabinet to examine “all possible ways” to tackle the cost of living crisis.
On his first full day in power, the prime minister faced questions about how he would fund the removal of VAT from electricity bills and an expected uplift in defence spending – an issue that led his new chancellor, John Healey, to resign as Keir Starmer’s defence secretary last month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham urges cabinet to examine ‘all possible ways’ to tackle cost of living crisis

articles.author: AFP
articles.description:
Parliament votes to stop children using apps such as TikTok in policy championed by Emmanuel Macron
France’s parliament has approved a bill banning social media access for children under 15, making it the first EU country to bar children from apps such as TikTok.
The president, Emmanuel Macron, has championed the ban as a key reform of his final term in office and pledged to enforce it by September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: France becomes first EU country to ban social media access for under-15s

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah, Yohannes Lowe and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
Sarwar expected to be elevated to Lords to take up a ministerial post at revamped Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

Burnham to cut VAT on electricity bills in first cost-of-living move

António Costa, the president of the European council, said in a post on X that he held a “good” phone call with Andy Burnham last night, in which he said they agreed to “further strengthen” EU-UK relations and continue to cooperate to support Ukraine.
He said there was also discussion about “common geopolitical challenges facing Europe”, which could be a reference to many things, including energy prices soaring due to the US-Israel war on Iran, Europe’s trading and security relationship with Washington, the future of Nato, the continent facing a wave of hybrid warfare, driven by Russia, or the surge of national populism and backlash against immigration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anas Sarwar reportedly set to quit as Scottish Labour leader to be minister in Andy Burnham’s government – as it happened

articles.author: Rob Evans
articles.description:
Paul Condon tells spycops inquiry force failed to properly control unit which committed ‘horrendous’ abuses
A former Metropolitan police commissioner has admitted that the surveillance of the family of Stephen Lawrence by undercover officers was institutionally racist, the spycops inquiry has heard.
While Paul Condon was in command of the Metropolitan police in the 1990s, a controversial undercover unit spied on the family as they sought to persuade Scotland Yard to properly investigate Lawrence’s racist murder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former Met police chief admits surveillance of Stephen Lawrence’s family was institutionally racist

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Diligent, popular, unexpected pick for the Treasury has been given a straitjacket – and the job of funding PM’s policy promises
On the frequent occasions that John Healey would travel abroad as defence secretary, he was so determined to keep working he would get the crew to tether a desk to the inside of his military aircraft so he could read his papers.
His diligence is one reason why Andy Burnham, the new prime minister, made Healey his unexpected pick for chancellor on Monday. Allies say others include their shared commitment to re-industrialisation and devolution.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fiscal hawk or big spender – what kind of chancellor will John Healey be?

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Such technology solves problem of longer, thinner, energy-saving wings not fitting in airports around the world
Airbus has said it will test folding wings for the next generation of its bestselling planes, as the world’s largest planemaker races to work out the shape of future commercial aircraft by the end of the decade.
Longer, thinner wings made of light but strong composite materials offer the promise of energy savings but present a problem for manufacturers because they will not fit in airports around the world, many of which are already at or near full capacity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Airbus to test folding wings for next generation of bestselling planes

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Former PM’s supporters question pledge to end factional infighting after more than half his cabinet removed or demoted
Allies of Keir Starmer have questioned Andy Burnham’s pledge to end factional infighting after he removed or demoted more than half of the outgoing prime minister’s cabinet in his first reshuffle.
“This was a deeply factional cabinet reshuffle,” one said. “The idea it was anything else is ridiculous.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Starmer allies see ‘hint of retribution’ in Burnham reshuffle

articles.author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
articles.description:
Warning to shipping companies, on top of Iran’s chokehold on strait of Hormuz, may severely affect Saudi oil exports

Middle East crisis live – latest updates

Yemen’s Iranian-aligned Houthis have warned shipping companies that their tankers risk being attacked if they use Saudi Arabian ports, as the militia moved quickly to enforce a blockade announced the previous day.
The Houthi warning for the Red Sea, coming on top of Iran’s threat to shipping on the other side of the Arabian peninsular in the Gulf, could affect the substantial Saudi oil exports that have so far been unscathed by the months-long conflict and deepen the rapidly escalating crisis in the region.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Houthis threaten to attack shipping tankers if they use Saudi Arabian ports on Red Sea

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Thousands of people again on the streets of Delhi calling for education reforms despite police violence on Monday
Taru had come to the protest prepared this time. In one hand was an anti-government poster and in the other was a bicycle helmet. “We need to have protection in case Delhi police beat us up again,” said the 25-year-old, who stood among her friends. “We are not scared of them and we won’t run away, no matter what they do. We’ll stay here till they listen.”
On Tuesday, central Delhi still thronged with thousands of protesters, as an unprecedented expression of dissent against the powerful ruling Narendra Modi government showed no sign of abating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: India’s Cockroach movement protesters show no sign of backing down

articles.author: Dan Sabbagh Defence and security editor
articles.description:
New defence secretary Wes Streeting denounces drill by Neustrashimy as ‘performative and irresponsible’
A Russian warship fired its main cannon in a short notice test 45 miles south of Plymouth on Monday, the day Andy Burnham was appointed as prime minister.
The Neustrashimy suddenly announced it intended to fire its guns in the morning and requested that a British warship, which had been tracking it, retreat a couple of miles to a safe distance.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Russian warship carries out rare live-fire exercise 45 miles off UK coast

articles.author: Agence France-Presse
articles.description:
Meliá group says Donald Trump’s sanctions make it ‘impossible’ to keep any of its 34 sites open
A Spanish hotel chain is to cease all operations in Cuba at the end of the week due to “major difficulties” in doing business on the island under growing pressure from Washington.
The latest US sanctions make it “impossible, de facto and de jure, to maintain even minimal operational stability”, the Meliá group explained in a statement on Tuesday to the Spanish stock market regulator.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Spanish hotel chain ceases operations in Cuba under pressure from Washington

articles.author: Ellie Violet Bramley
articles.description:
Film star promotes Christopher Nolan film epic wearing gold artefacts dating back almost 3,000 years
The Odyssey is a story about a Greek king’s long journey home. But a pair of earrings worn on the new film adaptation’s press tour – and their long separation from their homeland – is sparking controversy.
At a photocall in London, Zendaya, who plays the goddess Athena in the Christopher Nolan film, wore a pair of earrings fashioned from Iranian artefacts dating back to 700BC.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Zendaya faces backlash for wearing ancient Iranian jewellery at Odyssey event

articles.author: Patrick Commins Economics editor
articles.description:
Experts warn global energy market at a ‘critical juncture’ with escalating Middle East crisis expected to further drag on a slowing Australian economy

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The likelihood of a Reserve Bank interest rate hike has doubled, according to market forecasts, as the escalating Middle East crisis once again drives fuel prices higher amid dwindling global oil reserves.
The total breakdown in the fragile ceasefire between the US and Iran has sent the international Brent crude benchmark surging by 23% over the past two weeks and back within reach of $US90 a barrel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: RBA now twice as likely to hike interest rates as US-Iran war drives fuel prices higher

articles.author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
articles.description:
The former Rudd/Gillard government minister has a plan for fighting back against populists including Pauline Hanson

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The incoming Labor president, Kate Ellis, says toxicity in politics is spilling into the broader community and public debate, warning that threats against MPs’ safety are limiting how elected politicians do their jobs.
Due to succeed Wayne Swan as the leader of Labor’s organisational base at this week’s national conference, the former Rudd/Gillard government minister said fighting back against populists including Pauline Hanson was best achieved by demonstrating policies that improve voters’ lives.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Kate Ellis is back – and the heat of political debate is higher than ever, incoming Labor president says

articles.author: Ben Smee Queensland correspondent
articles.description:
Exclusive: Leaked document from LNP-convened panel heavily criticises police responses to family violence and calls for civilian oversight

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Queensland government has buried the findings of its own working group of domestic violence victim-survivors after their report was heavily critical of police responses and called for a “civilian review mechanism” to escalate complaints about police.
The Liberal National government has repeatedly said it would “put victims at the heart” of the state’s justice policies.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The Queensland government promised to put victims first. But it has buried a report from domestic violence survivors

articles.author: Miranda Bryant Nordic correspondent
articles.description:
Government urges visitors not to approach or feed wolves as it manages safety amid growing population
Danish authorities have advised tourists to stand still, make eye contact and put up “maximum resistance” in the event of attack if they encounter a wolf while on holiday.
After a 200-year absence, wolves started returning to Denmark in 2012. There are now estimated to be 49 wolves on the Danish peninsula of Jutland.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Stand still, make eye contact: Denmark tells tourists how to behave in a wolf encounter

articles.author: Ruaridh Nicoll in Havana
articles.description:
State department’s 100-page report is latest push in Trump administration campaign to bring down government
The US government’s latest allegations that Cuba is behind “many of the most significant upheavals in recent American political history” and that its leaders pose “a unique threat to American homeland security” have come as startling revelations to those living under the six-month-long US oil blockade in Havana, where desperate people search through piles of uncollected rubbish for food, or else swelter at home in 24-hour-plus blackouts.
The unsigned 100-page report, Cuba: Capital of 21st-Century Communism, published by the US state department on Monday, blames Havana for everything from “the George Floyd riots to the rise of antifa to the explosion of pro-terrorist activism on American college campuses”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: US claims of Cuba’s ‘unique threat’ jar with reality of hunger and blackouts

articles.author: Olivia Bowden in Toronto
articles.description:
Chiefs in Ontario say they were left to self-evacuate before homes burned to ground, after being told there was no imminent threat
Fast-moving wildfires have burned two First Nations communities in Canada to the ground, as members said they were left to self-evacuate without government help or emergency alerts.
Thirteen communities in Ontario province have been ordered to evacuate because of wildfires, most of them First Nations. The Ontario premier, Doug Ford, told reporters on Monday that close to 2,000 people had been evacuated so far to cities including Toronto and Niagara Falls.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: We received no alert, say leaders of First Nations communities razed by Canadian wildfires

articles.author: Associated Press  in Kabul
articles.description:
National disaster agency confirms ‘severe financial and human losses’ in eastern  province of Nuristan
Rescue crews in Afghanistan are searching for survivors and bodies among the rubble of houses destroyed by devastating flash floods that authorities said had killed nearly two dozen people and left more than 100 people missing.
The Afghanistan national disaster management authority said on Tuesday that 23 people had died, 80 had been injured and more than 100 were missing after floods struck the eastern province of Nuristan on Monday, causing an undetermined number of buildings to collapse. The provincial capital city of Parun was among the areas affected, authorities said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Rescuers in Afghanistan search for missing and dead after flash floods destroy homes

articles.author: Andrew Roth and Sufian Taha in Deir Jarir
articles.description:
Residents of Deir Jarir say raids that killed two Palestinians late on Sunday are part of pattern of violence
Even by the brutal standards of militant settler violence in the West Bank, the raid on Deir Jarir late on Sunday night that killed two Palestinians and left another in hospital with a gunshot wound was extreme.
Palestinians in the town said settlers from a nearby outpost arrived after 9pm on Sunday claiming that they were searching for stolen livestock. Israeli soldiers and police soon joined them, protecting them as they sought to take several villagers’ sheep by force.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: IDF accused of working with settlers after latest deadly West Bank raid

articles.author: Kat Lay Global health correspondent
articles.description:
Global hunger declined for the third year in a row in 2025 but experts call for action to bring down costs of fruit, vegetables and dairy as report shows 2.69bn people can’t afford to eat well
One in three people cannot afford to eat a healthy diet, a new report has found, prompting calls for urgent action on food affordability.
There are 2.69 billion people unable to afford a diverse diet that meets their energy and nutrient needs, and it will take “immense” amounts of work to achieve the global target of zero hunger by 2030, the annual report from five UN agencies warned.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Healthy diet too expensive for one in three people globally, UN report finds

articles.author: Hannah Ellis-Petersen in Delhi
articles.description:
Youth-led group calls on education minister to quit in one of India’s largest anti-government rallies in years

Tens of thousands of protesters have defied police orders and descended on Delhi to demand the resignation of India’s education minister in one of the largest anti-government demonstrations in years.
A huge crowd, largely made up of students and gen Z-ers, filled the streets in the heart of India’s capital from early Monday morning shouting anti-government slogans. Hundreds had already camped out overnight.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tens of thousands of Cockroach movement protesters defy police with Delhi march

articles.author: Sarah Basford Canales
articles.description:
Many of the more than 100 people awaiting processing on the tiny Pacific island are skipping meals to make ends meet, a new survey has found

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Most refugees and asylum seekers held in Nauru’s detention centres say they cannot afford to buy enough food or access clean drinking water, despite the Australian government spending the equivalent of more than $9m per person last financial year.
The group of more than 100 people have been sent indefinitely to the tiny Pacific island while they wait for their asylum claims to be processed. Many of the cohort say they are skipping meals to make ends meet, according to a new survey by the Asylum Seeker Resource Centre (ASRC) advocacy group.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia spent more than $9m for each asylum seeker held on Nauru last year – so why can’t they afford to buy food?

articles.author: Carmen Aguilar García and Antonio Voce in London; Hannah Ellis-Petersen and Aakash Hassan in Delhi
articles.description:
Exclusive: Outdoor workers losing up to 9% of income as weather becomes ‘poverty multiplier’, research says
Extreme heat is pushing some of India’s poorest workers further into poverty, with income losses of up to 9% for outdoor workers, new research has found.
Analysis done by the International Institute for Environment and Development (IIED), and shared exclusively with the Guardian, found that extreme heat is acting as a “poverty multiplier” for hundreds of millions of workers in India’s informal sector.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘When I get home, my whole body aches’: extreme heat saps health and wages of India’s poorest workers

articles.author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan
articles.description:
Incumbent Carlos Vila Nova hopes to defeat his former party and secure second term as independent
Voters in São Tomé and Príncipe go to the polls for a presidential election on Sunday as one of Africa’s least populous countries seeks to burnish its democratic credentials.
According to the National Election Commission, about 142,000 people are registered to vote in the tiny African state’s elections, approximately 15% of whom live in the diaspora.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: São Tomé and Príncipe heads to polls in tense presidential election

articles.author: Carlos Mureithi in Greater Accra
articles.description:
Hand-painted works are often wildly unfaithful to the movies they portray – reinterpretations that sometimes resulted in threats, insults and even physical attacks from viewers who felt duped
Sitting on his porch in Teshie near Accra, Heavy J dipped a brush into red oil paint and dabbed it carefully on to his canvas – a flour sack – adding blood to a knife being wielded by a man. Higher on the canvas, he had started on an outline of a skull.
Heavy J was creating a poster, but not as you might have expected for a horror film. Instead, it was for the animated fairytale The Little Mermaid. The man with the knife was not a killer but the film’s kind-hearted prince, Eric. The skull was also unrelated to the story. “We add more to make people interested,” said Heavy J, whose real name is Jeaurs Affutu.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘We are preserving a tradition’: how Ghana’s sensationalist film posters became collectible art

articles.author: Petra Stock and Associated Press
articles.description:
Distillery owner could face only three months in jail over alleged poisoning of Australian teenagers

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Australian government has increased its travel alert level for Laos, advising travellers to “exercise a high degree of caution” due to the risk of methanol poisoning.
It comes as a distillery owner in Laos was charged after a mass methanol poisoning incident killed six foreign nationals, including the Australian backpackers Bianca Jones and Holly Morton-Bowles.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Australia updates travel advice for Laos as charges announced over mass methanol poisoning

articles.author: Vandy Widyalankara
articles.description:
Escaped flowerhorn cichlids are causing concern for native species and about parasites capable of infecting humans
Escaped ornamental aquarium fish have integrated into a local ecosystem in the Philippines, but scientists say they may be threatening the native biodiversity of the lake.
Flowerhorn cichlids – human-bred hybrid fish prized for their bright-gold colour and prominent head humps – are believed to have escaped from breeding facilities into Lake Sampaloc, which sits in a volcanic crater, during a typhoon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Biodiversity fears as human-bred hybrid fish integrate into Philippines lake

articles.author: Reuters
articles.description:
Aid workers are first known people to quarantine at facility, which sparked huge opposition in Kenya 
Seven American aid workers who had been in Congo to fight the Ebola outbreak are quarantining at a new isolation facility in ⁠Kenya after the US government introduced travel ⁠restrictions, the head of a US charity ​employing them told Reuters.
The aid workers are the first known people to quarantine at the facility, which has sparked huge opposition in Kenya and is at the heart of a legal case in which a court has ordered the work to be ⁠suspended. Construction continued, however, according to US officials and satellite imagery reviewed by Reuters.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Seven Americans quarantining at Kenya Ebola facility after US travel ban, says aid group

articles.author: Amy Hawkins Senior China correspondent
articles.description:
Arrest in Pennsylvania of Wu Shaoping, who is awaiting asylum decision, raises fears of deportation and persecution
A Chinese human rights lawyer has been arrested by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), raising concerns he could be deported to China where he would face persecution.
Wu Shaoping fled China at the end of 2019 amid a crackdown on human rights lawyers. He travelled to the US on a tourist visa and made an asylum claim in 2020, for which he is still awaiting a decision.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ICE arrests human rights lawyer who fled Chinese crackdown

articles.author: Magdalena Shopova for MetDesk
articles.description:
Storms are typical during intense heat but this week’s have been extreme. Plus, deadly monsoon rains in Bangladesh
Hailstones the size of golf balls have been seen in French villages as, on top of the exceptional European heatwave, thunderstorms have struck across parts of Europe.
While thunderstorms are typical during and after a period of extreme heat, the storms across countries such as France, Germany and Poland have been particularly severe, bringing flooding, strong winds and heavy showers with large balls of hail.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Weather tracker: Thunderstorms strike across Europe amid record heatwave

articles.author: Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Republicans also picked nominees in key congressional and statewide contests as both parties prepare for a high-stakes midterm battle in the battleground state



 Arizona voters on Tuesday chose their nominees for governor, Congress and other top offices, setting up a fall campaign that will test whether Republicans can reverse some of the Trump-era losses they suffered in a premier battleground state.
Andy Biggs, the hard-right congressman endorsed by Donald Trump, easily won the Republican nomination to challenge the incumbent Democrat, governor Katie Hobbs, in one of the most closely watched gubernatorial contests. 
Biggs, a former chair of the House freedom caucus who was a central figure in the effort to overturn Trump’s election loss in 2020, defeated fellow congressman David Schweikert, by appealing to the party’s deeply conservative base.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Biggs wins Republican primary for Arizona governor, setting up race against Katie Hobbs

articles.author: Chris Stein in Washington
articles.description:
Measure authorizes spending until 4 December as Republicans seek to avoid volatile issue in election season
The US House of Representatives on Tuesday approved a stopgap measure to head off a government shutdown until early December, with its Republican leaders seeking to defuse a volatile issue in the run-up to the November midterm elections.
The continuing resolution authorizing government spending until 4 December passed by a vote of 220-205, roughly along party lines. It next heads to the Senate, where it will need to win bipartisan support to clear the chamber.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House passes spending bill to head off government shutdown before midterms

articles.author: Robert Mackey, Shrai Popat, Maya Yang and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
This live blog is now closed.

Sign up for US Breaking News email

US gas prices have continued to rise since the conflict with Iran resumed this month. According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), a gallon of fuel is now just over $4 – almost a dollar more than a year ago.
It comes as Brent Crude, the international oil benchmark, is now up by almost 2% to $90.92 a barrel.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Trump announces new tariffs on generic drugs to take effect in 2028 – as it happened

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The second circuit overturned the previous decision, saying the judge overstepped authority by intervening before it moved through the immigration court system
A federal appeals panel has reversed a lower court decision ordering the release of pro-Palestinian activist Mohsen Mahdawi, opening the door to the re-arrest of a student protest organizer whom the Trump administration has spent more than a year trying to deport.
Tuesday’s ruling from the second US circuit court of appeals in New York City overturns a previous decision by a federal judge in Vermont, which likened the government’s efforts to expel him and other activists to McCarthyist repression.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Appeals court reverses decision that released pro-Palestinian Columbia activist Mohsen Mahdawi

articles.author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington and Lauren Gambino
articles.description:
Defense secretary has asked Senate appropriations committee for nearly $88bn more to continue effort
The US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth told the Senate on Tuesday that the US-Israel war on Iran had cost $37.5bn so far, as he faced lawmakers furious over the conflict’s soaring price tag and the deaths last week of three American service members.
During an appearance before the Senate appropriations committee, Hegseth, whose opening remarks were repeatedly interrupted by protesters, provided an updated account of the war’s cost – up from previous estimates – and defended the Trump administration’s roughly $88bn supplemental funding request, calling it “urgent, necessary”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hegseth tells Senate war on Iran has so far cost $37.5bn at hearing to request more funds

articles.author: Arwa Mahdawi
articles.description:
Once Republicans’ favourite punchline, Joe Biden’s son is now building an online following by trolling JD Vance, taunting Trump and embracing the absurdity of US politics
What sort of longshot candidate do we reckon is going to run for US president in 2028? The Rock? Kim Kardashian? Kermit the Frog? US politics has become so debased that being rich, famous and a natural-born citizen (sorry, Zohran Mamdani) now seem to be the only qualifications required for a job in the White House.
Which is why you shouldn’t entirely write off murmurings that Hunter Biden might be interested in following in his daddy’s presidential footsteps. When asked by a Fox News reporter about Hunter’s 2028 odds last month, Donald Trump suggested Joe Biden’s prodigal son might “do well”. If other “basket case[s]” in the Democratic party could do well, Trump added, then Hunter probably had a shot. Various analysts appear to agree. “Could Hunter Biden run for office? Don’t rule it out,” a recent Times headline blared. The article quotes a Biden biographer saying: “With a character like Hunter Biden in a populist, social media-driven political environment, you have to never say never.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Hunter Biden for president? Stranger things have happened | Arwa Mahdawi

articles.author: George Chidi in Memphis
articles.description:
The city rallied behind Tamboli’s despite online boycott calls, as frustration grows over the Trump administration’s federal taskforce following multiple deaths
You can measure the disconnect between angry internet commentariat and real life Memphis residents by the length of the wait for a table at Tamboli’s Pasta & Pizza.
In early July, Miles Tamboli, the owner of the midtown pizza spot, made a decision: he would not serve the national guard deployed to the city by the Trump administration, which the US president claimed would reduce the city’s crime rate. Tamboli’s video announcement came days after troops killed two city residents, bringing the total to four since the initiative started in September.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Buy-cott’ boosts Memphis pizza shop after owner refuses to serve national guard

articles.author: Bhaskar Sunkara
articles.description:
The congresswoman can run a serious national campaign on the left and pull a movement in behind it. She should get in early
In the summer of 2018, almost no one thought Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez could beat Joe Crowley. Crowley was a 10-term incumbent, the fourth-ranking Democrat in the House, a man some thought would one day be speaker. A 28-year-old former bartender and democratic socialist was the longest of long shots to succeed him. But ever since she did, the political establishment has been trying to decide whether to take her seriously.
For a while it decided not to. The Missouri representative Emanuel Cleaver said the Democratic caucus did not need her “sniping”, while the then senator Claire McCaskill dismissed her as a “bright and shiny new object”. Ocasio-Cortez seemed to enjoy the response. Asked on 60 Minutes whether she wanted people to underestimate her, she said: “Absolutely. That’s how I won my primary.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez should run for president | Bhaskar Sunkara

articles.author: Natasha Lennard
articles.description:
Yotam Marom, who helped lead Occupy Wall Street, discusses why power must be built through movements, not simply through elected officials
Yotam Marom knows why the Occupy Wall Street movement fell apart 15 years ago. The New York-based organizer and author was a key participant in the nationwide constellation of encampments and rolling protests that brought tens of thousands of people into its fold. But the movement could not withstand police raids, evictions, a bitter winter and, as Marom sees it, an internal “politics of powerlessness”, which mistook a healthy distrust of institutional power for a failure to build a strong, coherent strategy for political change. Occupy splintered within a few short months and never seriously revived.
As he recounts in his new book, For Louder Days: Reaching Beyond a Politics of Powerlessness, Marom has again and again seen similar dynamics weigh down social movements in his work as an organizer and facilitator. He founded the Wildfire Project, a training organization for grassroots groups, and has worked with organizations including the Sunrise Movement agitating against climate decimation, the abolitionist Dream Defenders fighting for racial justice, the Uncommitted movement to end Democratic party support for Israel’s war crimes, tenants unions battling landlords, and more.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From Bernie to Mamdani, how the Occupy movement transformed American politics

articles.author: Martin Pengelly
articles.description:
Historian Kim Phillips-Fein’s book Country of Lords looks back at the many men who have tried to fight against egalitarianism, from John Adams to Peter Thiel
The historian Kim Phillips-Fein’s new book is published amid celebrations of the 250th anniversary of the declaration of independence and its truth “self-evident, that all men are created equal”. Country of Lords, however, is a history of Neo-Aristocrats, Social Darwinists, Tech Utopians, and the Long Fight Against Equality in America.
Concise and hard-hitting, the book arrives at a time of glaring social and economic inequality, Phillips-Fein seeing Elon Musk “emerging as a trillionaire very much on people’s minds, with a deep level of discomfort, both fear and anger about what this portends”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Social Darwinists to tech bros: tracing the long fight against equality in US

articles.author: Will Craft and Andrew Witherspoon
articles.description:
The Guardian has reviewed figures from Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection since Trump’s inauguration
Donald Trump campaigned on a platform of mass deportation. Since he took office, his administration has reshaped immigration enforcement across the country. The Guardian, using data published every two weeks by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), is tracking the number of people the administration has arrested, detained and deported.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: By the numbers: the latest ICE and CBP data on arrests, detentions and deportations in the US

articles.author: Robert Reich
articles.description:
As Todd Blanche, Erica Schwartz and Jay Clayton face the Senate,  a fundamental disconnect becomes clear
There’s been a lot of discussion in America this week about the meaning of integrity.
You didn’t hear the word used directly; it was alluded to indirectly – in wondering whether Lindsey Graham was an immoral opportunist or clever pragmatist; in suspecting Todd Blanche of being more loyal to Trump than to the nation; in distrusting Erica Schwartz, Trump’s latest pick to lead the CDC, when she said she would never compromise on the science; in doubting Jay Clayton, his pick for director of national intelligence, will tell Trump anything he doesn’t want to hear.
Robert Reich, a former US secretary of labor, is a professor of public policy emeritus at the University of California, Berkeley. He is a Guardian US columnist and his newsletter is at robertreich.substack.com. His new book, Coming Up Short: A Memoir of My America, is out now in the US and in the UK
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The trouble with Trump’s latest nominees lies in one word: integrity | Robert Reich

articles.author: Norman Solomon
articles.description:
More than 100 Democratic lawmakers voted against arms for Israel. They’re listening to the people – their bosses are behind
The Democratic party is in dire need of a mutiny.
Top leaders at the party’s helm are unprepared to navigate the political sea change about Israel. Last week, nearly half of House Democrats voted to block $3.3bn in weaponry and other aid to that country. A recent New York Times poll found that 74% of Democratic voters “opposed providing additional economic and military support to Israel, including large majorities in all age groups”.
Norman Solomon is the director of RootsAction and executive director of the Institute for Public Accuracy. His latest book is The Blue Road to Trump Hell: How Corporate Democrats Paved the Way for Autocracy
 Continue reading...
articles.title: House Democrats are finally shifting on Israel. Party leaders must listen | Norman Solomon

articles.author: Sam Levine Zhara Keogh Michael Kalenderian Sarah Bertram
articles.description:
Donald Trump delivered a primetime address to the country on Thursday, claiming that declassified intelligence showed Chinese interference in US elections. The US president revived long-running attacks on election security, despite a US intelligence assessment that found no evidence Beijing altered the 2020 vote, which he lost. The Guardian's voting rights reporter Sam Levine factchecks some of Trump's claims

Trump is invoking foreign election interference to justify his own - Opinion

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fact-checking Donald Trump’s address on Chinese election interference – video

articles.author: Hosted by Jonathan Freedland . Produced by May Robson, Jacob Liebenberg, Ned Carter Miles and the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj .
articles.description:
The debate about how old is too old to serve in public office has resurfaced this week after the shock death of the Republican senator Lindsey Graham and the surprise return of Mitch McConnell, the 84-year-old senator who published a photo of himself in hospital after a long absence from the spotlight.
With rumours continuing to swirl around Donald Trump’s health, why is it US politicians seem to cling on to power for so long?
Jonathan Freedland speaks to Alexis Coe, a presidential historian and columnist for the New York Times Book review, about whether the US is becoming a gerontocracy – and what can be done about it
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Are American politicians too old? | Politics Weekly America

articles.author: Hosted by Kai Wright and Carter Sherman , with Shrai Popat and Lauren Gambino . Produced by Meg Driscoll, edited by Anabel Bacon , engineered by Ivan Kuraev
articles.description:
Earlier this week, Graham Platner, the Democratic candidate for Senate in Maine, was accused by a former partner of sexual assault. Platner denies the allegations, but on Wednesday, he suspended his campaign, accusing the “political establishment” of tanking his candidacy. But this is only the most recent scandal to have surfaced around Platner’s campaign — over the past year, the oyster farmer and combat veteran was revealed to have a tattoo that closely resembled a Totenkopf (a widely recognized Nazi symbol), a long paper trail of racist, misogynist and homophobic posts on Reddit, and in June, the New York Times published allegations from three former partners about Platner’s “toxic” behavior in their relationships, including, in several cases, physical intimidation (allegations Platner denied).
As Democrats regroup and evaluate their dwindling chances to flip the Senate in November, hosts Kai Wright and Carter Sherman are joined by Guardian political reporters Lauren Gambino and Shrai Popat to ask why voters flocked to Platner, why they were reluctant to abandon him as the scandals came out — and what the whole mess says about who gets the privilege of political redemption.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Why Graham Platner wasn’t the answer to the Democrats’ man problem – Stateside with Kai and Carter

articles.author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Matt Hughes ; produced by Annie La Vespa and Leonore Schick ; senior producer Ryan Ramgobin
articles.description:
There is just one week to go until the winner of the World Cup is crowned, and it has been a memorable tournament, not least due to the extraordinary intervention by Donald Trump this week that shocked the football world. Lucy Hough speaks to global sports business correspondent Matt Hughes
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How Trump’s intervention tarnished the World Cup – The Latest

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
UK resident was evacuated from Democratic Republic of the Congo where there is an outbreak of the disease
A humanitarian worker is being monitored at a specialist hospital in London after potential exposure to the Ebola virus.
The UK resident was medically evacuated from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) where the worker had been treating patients with the disease, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Health worker monitored for Ebola in London hospital after working in DRC

articles.author: Kiran Stacey and Peter Walker
articles.description:
As new prime minister briefs cabinet on ‘cost of living government’, critics ask where money will come from
Andy Burnham is under mounting pressure to explain how he will pay for his policy pledges as he implored his new cabinet to examine “all possible ways” to tackle the cost of living crisis.
On his first full day in power, the prime minister faced questions about how he would fund the removal of VAT from electricity bills and an expected uplift in defence spending – an issue that led his new chancellor, John Healey, to resign as Keir Starmer’s defence secretary last month.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham urges cabinet to examine ‘all possible ways’ to tackle cost of living crisis

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah, Yohannes Lowe and Tom Ambrose
articles.description:
Sarwar expected to be elevated to Lords to take up a ministerial post at revamped Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade

Burnham to cut VAT on electricity bills in first cost-of-living move

António Costa, the president of the European council, said in a post on X that he held a “good” phone call with Andy Burnham last night, in which he said they agreed to “further strengthen” EU-UK relations and continue to cooperate to support Ukraine.
He said there was also discussion about “common geopolitical challenges facing Europe”, which could be a reference to many things, including energy prices soaring due to the US-Israel war on Iran, Europe’s trading and security relationship with Washington, the future of Nato, the continent facing a wave of hybrid warfare, driven by Russia, or the surge of national populism and backlash against immigration.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anas Sarwar reportedly set to quit as Scottish Labour leader to be minister in Andy Burnham’s government – as it happened

articles.author: Rob Evans
articles.description:
Paul Condon tells spycops inquiry force failed to properly control unit which committed ‘horrendous’ abuses
A former Metropolitan police commissioner has admitted that the surveillance of the family of Stephen Lawrence by undercover officers was institutionally racist, the spycops inquiry has heard.
While Paul Condon was in command of the Metropolitan police in the 1990s, a controversial undercover unit spied on the family as they sought to persuade Scotland Yard to properly investigate Lawrence’s racist murder.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Former Met police chief admits surveillance of Stephen Lawrence’s family was institutionally racist

articles.author: Source: Reuters
articles.description:
The prime minister told his new cabinet in its first meeting that the government will be a 'cost-of-living government' and needs to examine 'all possible ways' to help families struggling with high costs. The new prime minister announced an £850m tax cut on electricity bills in his first significant policy announcement
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham to cut tax on electricity to ease cost of living - video

articles.author: Kiran Stacey Policy editor
articles.description:
Diligent, popular, unexpected pick for the Treasury has been given a straitjacket – and the job of funding PM’s policy promises
On the frequent occasions that John Healey would travel abroad as defence secretary, he was so determined to keep working he would get the crew to tether a desk to the inside of his military aircraft so he could read his papers.
His diligence is one reason why Andy Burnham, the new prime minister, made Healey his unexpected pick for chancellor on Monday. Allies say others include their shared commitment to re-industrialisation and devolution.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Fiscal hawk or big spender – what kind of chancellor will John Healey be?

articles.author: Jasper Jolly
articles.description:
Such technology solves problem of longer, thinner, energy-saving wings not fitting in airports around the world
Airbus has said it will test folding wings for the next generation of its bestselling planes, as the world’s largest planemaker races to work out the shape of future commercial aircraft by the end of the decade.
Longer, thinner wings made of light but strong composite materials offer the promise of energy savings but present a problem for manufacturers because they will not fit in airports around the world, many of which are already at or near full capacity.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Airbus to test folding wings for next generation of bestselling planes

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Former PM’s supporters question pledge to end factional infighting after more than half his cabinet removed or demoted
Allies of Keir Starmer have questioned Andy Burnham’s pledge to end factional infighting after he removed or demoted more than half of the outgoing prime minister’s cabinet in his first reshuffle.
“This was a deeply factional cabinet reshuffle,” one said. “The idea it was anything else is ridiculous.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Starmer allies see ‘hint of retribution’ in Burnham reshuffle

articles.author: Steven Morris
articles.description:
James Desborough told court he had discovered bodies of Claudio Aquilino and Daniel Coleman on his land near St Austell
A convicted killer accused of murdering two of his friends whose remains were found burnt and dismembered near his Cornish woodland cabin has insisted he did not kill them but had discovered their bodies on his land.
James Desborough claimed he came upon one of the bodies hanging from a tree and the second lying naked in a stream.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Convicted killer denies murdering two friends whose remains were found near his Cornwall cabin

articles.author: Damian Carrington Environment editor
articles.description:
A ‘reasonable worst-case scenario’ suggests need for large-scale movement of populations away from reshaped coast
Up to 13 million people in the UK face the long-term risk of coastal flooding due to the climate crisis, scientists have warned, with a “reasonable worst-case scenario” suggesting the need for the large-scale movement of populations away from a dramatically reshaped coast.
Even if today’s global pledges to cut carbon pollution are met, about 1.4 million more people will be exposed to coastal floods in 2200 and 1.7 million in 2300 due to the sea level rise driven by melting ice caps and warming oceans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Millions face long-term coastal flooding risk in UK without climate action, scientists warn

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Durham University researchers find cataclysmic direct hit with Gaia Sausage sent Milky Way into its current position
Astronomers have found evidence that the Milky Way was flipped on its side following a direct hit from a wayward galaxy long before the solar system was born.
The cataclysmic collision took place about 10bn years ago when the Milky Way was struck head-on by an incoming dwarf galaxy known – for purely astronomical reasons – as the Gaia Sausage.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Milky Way flipped in collision with dwarf galaxy 10bn years ago, astronomers say

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news
More on the cost of living: new figures show that UK grocery inflation eased in the four weeks to 12th July to 2.6%, its lowest rate since December 2024.
It marks the fifth consecutive month of slowing price rises, Worldpanel by Numerator found.
Easing price rises will come as welcome news to shoppers, but the annual bill tells a fuller story. The average household spent £5,530 on groceries over the past twelve months to July, up £156 on the same period last year - a reminder that even as the rate of inflation cools, the cumulative cost of the weekly shop keeps climbing.
L&VW agrees that there is an opportunity to enhance the way local government, regulators and Thames Water work together, granting greater public controls on critical business issues to improve delivery of complex, essential infrastructure projects, and demonstrate shared accountability.
The consortium is willing to make significant new commitments to grant greater controls and oversight to ministers, implemented through a ‘golden share’.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Oil price rises above $90 as US and Iran exchange fire and Houthis threaten naval blockade in Saudi Arabia - as it happened

articles.author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
articles.description:
Office of Prime Minister and Cabinet, led by Louise Haigh, will oversee both No 10 in London and Manchester

Burnham’s first cabinet: who’s in and who’s out?

Andy Burnham has created a powerful new prime minister’s department taking in parts of the Cabinet Office, Treasury and housing ministry to become the “dominant driver of the UK’s economy”.
In one of his first acts, Burnham has created the Office of the Prime Minister and Cabinet, to be led by his ally and enforcer Louise Haigh, which will oversee the No 10 operation in London, the forthcoming No 10 North in Manchester and parts of the Cabinet Office.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham shakes up Whitehall with new government department

articles.author: Hilary Osborne and Jillian Ambrose
articles.description:
New prime minister is implementing immediate tax cut to help ease cost of living pressures for British households

Andy Burnham to cut VAT on electricity bills as first cost of living move

Household electricity bills for people in Great Britain will not attract VAT for six months, under the first of a series of cost of living measures announced by the new prime minister, Andy Burnham.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What will Andy Burnham’s VAT cut on electricity bills mean for you?

articles.author: Mark Sweney
articles.description:
Move would give government veto over big decisions and hostile takeovers, after Burnham’s call for greater public control

Nils Pratley: Burnham has forced greater clarity at Thames Water. Now he must choose

The group of investors pursuing a rescue bid for Thames Water have offered the government a “golden share” in a last-ditch attempt to persuade Andy Burnham not to nationalise Britain’s biggest water company.
London & Valley Water (L&VW), a consortium of 100 institutional investors that hold £17bn of the company’s £21bn debt, said it recognised the new prime minister wanted greater public control and to strengthen the accountability of the water company.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Thames Water investors offer ‘golden share’ in bid to head off nationalisation

articles.author: Jennifer Rankin in Brussels and Lisa O’Carroll in London
articles.description:
European leaders have made positive noises about the new UK PM, but he is likely to face the same restrictions as Starmer

UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham is unknown in Brussels, but that will soon change. In his schedule for the autumn is an EU-UK summit that may underscore the same dilemmas that have confronted previous British prime ministers in the relationship with Europe.
EU leaders were quick to offer congratulations to Britain’s prime minister, the seventh since the 2016 Brexit referendum. The European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said she looked forward to strengthening the EU-UK partnership “for the security of our shared continent” and “the prosperity of people on both sides of the Channel”. The German chancellor, Friedrich Merz, invited Burnham to visit Berlin “very soon”, noting that the UK and Germany’s “deep connection is particularly evident in these times”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: What the EU wants from Andy Burnham

articles.author: Damien Gayle
articles.description:
Millions of people in southern England and parts of Wales face restrictions after prolonged periods of hot weather
Millions of people across southern England are subject to hosepipe bans after prolonged periods of extreme heat and reduced rainfall. On Tuesday, Thames Water, Britain’s biggest water company, announced a ban starting on Thursday. Here, the Guardian answers questions about what the restriction means for you.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: How can I water my garden in a hosepipe ban and will there be drought this summer?

articles.author: Rowena Mason and Peter Walker
articles.description:
From the Treasury to the Home Office, we look at who is heading up key departments in new PM’s government

Burnham vows his arrival in power will be ‘circuit breaker’ moment for UK

Six highlights from Andy Burnham’s first Downing Street speech

Andy Burnham has appointed his first cabinet, with the new prime minister rewarding those who have been loyal to his takeover efforts. He had promised to pick his top team from all wings of the party in an effort to show he is trying to run a more inclusive administration.
But at the same time, his decision to have a brutal clearout of Starmer allies resulted in many considered to be on the right of the party or close to the former prime minister losing their jobs. These are the key announcements so far:
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Andy Burnham’s first Labour cabinet: who’s in and who’s out?

articles.author: Richard Partington Senior economics correspondent
articles.description:
Figure of £16bn from ONS comes after Andy Burnham revealed plans to cut VAT on electricity bills

Business live – latest updates

The UK government borrowed less than expected in June, in a boost for Andy Burnham as he set out plans to cut VAT on household electricity bills and promised a new direction for the British economy.
The Office for National Statistics (ONS) said public sector net borrowing – the difference between government spending and income – was £16bn last month, £7.9bn less than in June 2025.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK borrows less than expected as Healey vows to ‘buffer against uncertainty’

articles.author: Jon Henley Europe correspondent
articles.description:
Beyond the diplomatic platitudes global media focuses on the ‘immense’ scale of the challenge he faces in the job

UK politics live – latest updates

World leaders have warmly congratulated Andy Burnham on his entry into 10 Downing Street as Britain’s seventh prime minister in a decade, but international media largely focused on the scale of the challenges awaiting him.
Emmanuel Macron, France’s president, said he hoped for a deeper relationship “in the service of our peoples, and by giving new momentum to the partnership between the UK and the EU” rekindled by Burnham’s predecessor, Keir Starmer.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘A big job ahead of him’: world leaders congratulate Andy Burnham as he becomes Britain’s PM

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Babcock and BAE Systems benefit as markets hope former defence secretary will increase spending on sector

Business live – latest updates

Shares in defence companies have risen sharply after Andy Burnham appointed John Healey as chancellor, prompting hope among investors of increased spending on suppliers to the military.
Defence stocks were among the biggest risers on the FTSE 100 on Tuesday morning after the former defence secretary was announced as chancellor after markets closed on Monday. Babcock International rose 7%, BAE Systems was up 3% and Rolls-Royce increased nearly 2% on the FTSE 100. On the FTSE 250, QinetiQ rose nearly 4%.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Defence shares rise after Andy Burnham appoints John Healey as chancellor

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
Board of UK government contractor recommends deal with private-equity owned rival

Business live – latest updates

The outsourcer Mitie has agreed to a £3.1bn takeover by its private-equity owned rival OCS Group, ending nearly four decades on the stock market and making it the latest London-listed company to be acquired this year.
On Tuesday, the government contractor said its board has recommended that shareholders accept a cash offer of 221.6p a share, a 46.8% premium to Monday’s closing price.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Mitie agrees £3.1bn takeover by OCS in blow to London stock market

articles.author: Phillip Inman
articles.description:
Unemployment holds steady at 4.9%, underlining the challenge facing the new prime minister

Business live – latest updates

Employers cut the number of job vacancies in June, according to official figures that highlight the UK’s “fragile” economic outlook amid the conflict in the Middle East.
Job vacancies fell to 712,000 – almost half the level in 2022 – as employers put off hiring new staff in the three months to May, the Office for National Statistics said.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK employers cut job vacancies as Burnham aims to lift living standards

articles.author: Anna Tims
articles.description:
When the problem was finally sorted out in our new-build home, it increased my tariff by 19%
Residents in our new housing development are being billed for each other’s energy after the meters were mixed up.
I realised British Gas was sending bills for my energy to the developer of the estate instead of to me. I informed British Gas of my details when I moved in seven months ago.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: British Gas mixed up our energy meter – but now I’m being penalised

articles.author: Presented by Helen Pidd with Peter Walker and Paul Harrison; produced by Ruth Abrahams, Guy Szafman, Belinda Gurung and Rudi Zygadlo; the executive producer is Sami Kent
articles.description:
Senior political correspondent Peter Walker and former No 10 press secretary Paul Harrison analyse Andy Burnham’s first day as PM
On Monday, Andy Burnham finally realised his long-held ambition to become prime minister. But what problems can he expect to confront now he’s in No 10?
Former Downing Street press secretary Paul Harrison talks through the challenges of the office, from the awkward living arrangements to the even more awkward conversations with the president of the US. And senior political correspondent Peter Walker tells Helen Pidd about Burnham’s first speech at Downing Street, his new cabinet, and what it tells us about his plans in power.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Burnham begins: what awaits the new British PM? - podcast

articles.author: Mark Brown North of England correspondent
articles.description:
Revamped Ripon attraction reopens as a more immersive experience telling ‘national story’ of poverty and welfare
Visitors to one of Britain’s most complete surviving Victorian workhouses won’t have to strip and bathe in someone else’s bath water. But they might get some gruel, they can sweep the yard and there are “schoolmaster” volunteers happy to tell children how to behave.
“You are literally going to walk in the footsteps of people who have experienced this place,” said the director of the Ripon Museums Trust, Alexa Vernon.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Gruel and graft: museum asks if you could survive a Victorian workhouse
